Below is a single, consolidated 12‑week summary you can hand to your client. It integrates the revised strength program (3×/week with Phase 2 higher intensity), cardio (aerobic base + HIIT), 1×/week plyometric/power session, cycle-awareness for severe primary dysmenorrhea (no high‑intensity, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping on cycle days 1–3), a nutrition plan focused on fatigue/cramping, and guidance for a 1RM test at Phase‑3 end. Start date: 2026‑06‑01. I’ve included calendar notes for predicted flow windows so you can plan around them.

Key client facts and constraints
- 28 years old, recreational lifter, feeling stronger and wants more intensity.
- Regular 28‑day cycle. Last period started 2026‑05‑01.
- Flow days 1–3 are debilitating; on those days she must avoid:
  - High‑intensity exercise (HIIT, tempo intervals),
  - Heavy Valsalva (avoid maximal breath‑holding; no maximal singles that require Valsalva),
  - Jumping / plyometrics.
- GP cleared exercise; continue to monitor symptoms and consult GP / pelvic physio if symptoms worsen.

Predicted period start dates during the 12 weeks
- 2026‑06‑26 → flow 06‑26–06‑28 (Week 4)
- 2026‑07‑24 → flow 07‑24–07‑26 (Week 8)
- 2026‑08‑21 → flow 08‑21–08‑23 (Week 12)
Note: I’ve aligned deload weeks with these flow weeks so heavy work and plyos/HIIT fall on non‑flow days where possible.

Weekly training structure (default schedule)
- Mon: Strength A — Heavy Lower (main squat or variation)
- Tue: Cardio — Zone 2 steady (build aerobic base) or low‑impact recovery on flow
- Wed: Strength B — Heavy Upper
- Thu: HIIT (metabolic conditioning) — only on non‑flow days; swap for Zone 1 recovery on flow
- Fri: Strength C — Dynamic/Hypertrophy (posterior chain emphasis)
- Sat: Plyometric / Power session — only on non‑flow days; swap for low‑impact power on flow
- Sun: Rest / mobility / long easy Zone 1–2 walk or optional easy swim

Progression overview
- Mesocycle A — Base & Technique (Weeks 1–4; 2026‑06‑01 → 06‑28)
  - Strength: moderate loads (65–75% 1RM), 4×5 or similar; build technique and volume.
  - Cardio: Zone 2 sessions 25–35 min; Zone 1 recovery sessions.
  - Plyo: low volume, low‑impact power drills.
  - Week 4 is a deload (reduced volume/intensity ~40–50%). Flow days 06‑26–06‑28 — use flow‑day modifications for any training day that falls here (low intensity, no jumps, no heavy loads).
- Mesocycle B — Strength Focus (Weeks 5–8; 2026‑06‑29 → 07‑26) — intensified per your request
  - Strength: increased intensity:
    - Week 5: main lifts ~77–80% 1RM, 4×4–5
    - Week 6: ~82–85% 1RM, 5×3
    - Week 7: ~85–88% 1RM, 4–5×2–3 (heavy doubles/triples)
    - Week 8: deload 40–50% — aligns with flow 07‑24–07‑26 (do flow modifications)
  - Accessories: maintain hypertrophy volume 3×8–15 for resilience.
  - HIIT: maintained at 1×/week but moved off flow days; deload week swap.
  - Plyo: progress intensity on non‑flow days; deload/low‑impact on flow.
- Mesocycle C — Strength/Peaking & Maintenance (Weeks 9–12; 2026‑07‑27 → 08‑23)
  - Strength: heavier singles/doubles for peaking, but avoid 1RM attempts during flow week (Week 12 coincides with flow; see 1RM guidance).
  - Cardio: maintain Zone 2 volume and add tempo sessions on non‑flow days; Week 12 deload.
  - HIIT & Plyo: continue 1×/week each on non‑flow days; swap if they fall on flow days.
  - 1RM testing: possible in this period but only on non‑flow days and following taper guidance (details below).

Detailed weekly templates (examples of exercises, sets and reps)
- Strength A — Heavy Lower (Mon)
  - Mesocycle A example: Back squat 4×5 @ 65–70%; RDL 3×8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg; Pallof press 3×12; core work.
  - Mesocycle B progression: Week 5 squat 4×4 @77–80%; Week 6 5×3 @82–85%; Week 7 4×2–3 @85–88%; Week 8 deload 3×5 @60–65%.
  - Mesocycle C: squat heavy singles/doubles (5×3 → 4×2 etc.) depending on fatigue; keep accessory volume moderate.
  - Notes: Belt use and heavy Valsalva reserved only for non‑flow days if she uses them; always cue controlled exhale on exertion.

- Strength B — Heavy Upper (Wed)
  - Mesocycle A: Bench 4×6 @65%; Rows 4×8; OHP 3×8; accessories 3×12.
  - Mesocycle B: Bench progress to 4×4→5×3→4×2–3 at 77–88% as per week; maintain rows and OHP volume.
  - Mesocycle C: heavier bench singles/doubles in peaking weeks; deload as scheduled.

- Strength C — Dynamic / Posterior Chain + Hypertrophy (Fri)
  - Trap‑bar or conventional deadlift variations, hip thrusts, single‑leg RDLs, goblet/front squats; 3–5 sets, reps varying from 3–12 depending on phase.
  - Conditioning finisher: short Zone 1–2 bike 10–20 min (low impact).
  - Mesocycle B keeps heavier deadlift sets 5×3 @ ~80–82% in Week 6, then peaking week 4×2–3 at ~85–88% in Week 7; deload in Week 8.

Cardio plan (adds aerobic base)
- Frequency: 3 cardio sessions/week (2 steady + 1 HIIT). One long easy session optional on weekends.
- Zone 2 steady sessions: progressive increase from 25 min up to 50 min through the program with a deload every 4th week.
- HIIT: 1×/week, 20–30 min total session, only on non‑flow days. Examples:
  - Bike 8×20s work / 40s easy,
  - Row 6×45s work / 90s easy,
  - Pyramid intervals or EMOM combos.
- Flow days: restrict to Zone 1 walking, swimming, or gentle cycling for 15–30 min.

Plyometric / Power day (1×/week on Sat)
- Weeks 1–4: low volume, low‑impact power drills (medicine ball throws, low box jumps 15–30 cm or step‑downs, quick feet drills). Total jumps <12.
- Weeks 5–7: increase intensity on non‑flow days: drop jumps 20–30 cm, single‑leg bounds/hops (if comfortable), explosive trap‑bar shrugs — volume 12–20 quality attempts.
- Weeks 9–11: complex combos, med‑ball rotational throws, reactive drop jumps; maintain quality and safe landings.
- Week 8 and Week 12: deload and perform low‑impact alternatives if they coincide with flow (MB throws, band speed work, swim sprints).

Flow‑day modifications (any training during cycle days 1–3)
- Replace heavy lifts with:
  - Low‑load technical practice: bodyweight squats 3×10, banded hip hinges 3×12, glute bridges 3×15.
  - Low‑impact cardio: 15–30 min walking, easy cycling, or swimming (Zone 1).
  - Low‑impact power: medicine‑ball throws, light kettlebell swings, banded explosive step‑ups (no jumping).
  - Breathing & mobility: diaphragmatic breathing 5–10 min, pelvic floor awareness, heat pack recommendation.
- Do not perform HIIT, heavy singles requiring Valsalva, or plyometric jumps.

Nutrition plan summary (cycle‑aware; supports fatigue & cramping)
- Daily macronutrient guidance:
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily.
  - Fat: 25–35% of calories, emphasize omega‑3 sources (salmon, flax, walnuts).
  - Carbohydrates: periodized — higher on heavier training days and during follicular/luteal phases; slightly higher carbs on flow days to offset fatigue.
  - Calories: aim maintenance to slight surplus for recovery and strength gains. Avoid aggressive deficit, especially in luteal/menstrual window.
- Key nutrients and supplements (discuss with GP/RD):
  - Magnesium 200–400 mg at night may reduce cramps.
  - Omega‑3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA) may reduce pain/inflammation.
  - Iron only if labs indicate deficiency (check ferritin if heavy bleeding).
  - Vitamin D if deficient.
- Flow‑day eating strategies:
  - Warm meals, small frequent meals if nausea, focus on magnesium/iron rich foods, maintain hydration and electrolytes (salted broths if lightheaded).
  - Avoid excessive caffeine/alcohol around flow onset.
- Pre/post workout fueling:
  - Pre: small carb snack 30–60 min before higher‑intensity sessions.
  - Post: 20–40 g protein + carbs (30–60 g) after long or intense sessions.

HIIT integration & safety

- Tue: Cardio — Zone 2 steady (build aerobic base) or low‑impact recovery on flow
- Wed: Strength B — Heavy Upper
- Thu: HIIT (metabolic conditioning) — only on non‑flow days; swap for Zone 1 recovery on flow
- Fri: Strength C — Dynamic/Hypertrophy (posterior chain emphasis)
- Sat: Plyometric / Power session — only on non‑flow days; swap for low‑impact power on flow
- Sun: Rest / mobility / long easy Zone 1–2 walk or optional easy swim

Progression overview
- Mesocycle A — Base & Technique (Weeks 1–4; 2026‑06‑01 → 06‑28)
  - Strength: moderate loads (65–75% 1RM), 4×5 or similar; build technique and volume.
  - Cardio: Zone 2 sessions 25–35 min; Zone 1 recovery sessions.
  - Plyo: low volume, low‑impact power drills.
  - Week 4 is a deload (reduced volume/intensity ~40–50%). Flow days 06‑26–06‑28 — use flow‑day modifications for any training day that falls here (low intensity, no jumps, no heavy loads).
- Mesocycle B — Strength Focus (Weeks 5–8; 2026‑06‑29 → 07‑26) — intensified per your request
  - Strength: increased intensity:
    - Week 5: main lifts ~77–80% 1RM, 4×4–5
    - Week 6: ~82–85% 1RM, 5×3
    - Week 7: ~85–88% 1RM, 4–5×2–3 (heavy doubles/triples)
    - Week 8: deload 40–50% — aligns with flow 07‑24–07‑26 (do flow modifications)
  - Accessories: maintain hypertrophy volume 3×8–15 for resilience.
  - HIIT: maintained at 1×/week but moved off flow days; deload week swap.
  - Plyo: progress intensity on non‑flow days; deload/low‑impact on flow.
- Mesocycle C — Strength/Peaking & Maintenance (Weeks 9–12; 2026‑07‑27 → 08‑23)
  - Strength: heavier singles/doubles for peaking, but avoid 1RM attempts during flow week (Week 12 coincides with flow; see 1RM guidance).
  - Cardio: maintain Zone 2 volume and add tempo sessions on non‑flow days; Week 12 deload.
  - HIIT & Plyo: continue 1×/week each on non‑flow days; swap if they fall on flow days.
  - 1RM testing: possible in this period but only on non‑flow days and following taper guidance (details below).

Detailed weekly templates (examples of exercises, sets and reps)
- Strength A — Heavy Lower (Mon)
  - Mesocycle A example: Back squat 4×5 @ 65–70%; RDL 3×8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg; Pallof press 3×12; core work.
  - Mesocycle B progression: Week 5 squat 4×4 @77–80%; Week 6 5×3 @82–85%; Week 7 4×2–3 @85–88%; Week 8 deload 3×5 @60–65%.
  - Mesocycle C: squat heavy singles/doubles (5×3 → 4×2 etc.) depending on fatigue; keep accessory volume moderate.
  - Notes: Belt use and heavy Valsalva reserved only for non‑flow days if she uses them; always cue controlled exhale on exertion.

- Strength B — Heavy Upper (Wed)
  - Mesocycle A: Bench 4×6 @65%; Rows 4×8; OHP 3×8; accessories 3×12.
  - Mesocycle B: Bench progress to 4×4→5×3→4×2–3 at 77–88% as per week; maintain rows and OHP volume.
  - Mesocycle C: heavier bench singles/doubles in peaking weeks; deload as scheduled.

- Strength C — Dynamic / Posterior Chain + Hypertrophy (Fri)
  - Trap‑bar or conventional deadlift variations, hip thrusts, single‑leg RDLs, goblet/front squats; 3–5 sets, reps varying from 3–12 depending on phase.
  - Conditioning finisher: short Zone 1–2 bike 10–20 min (low impact).
  - Mesocycle B keeps heavier deadlift sets 5×3 @ ~80–82% in Week 6, then peaking week 4×2–3 at ~85–88% in Week 7; deload in Week 8.

Cardio plan (adds aerobic base)
- Frequency: 3 cardio sessions/week (2 steady + 1 HIIT). One long easy session optional on weekends.
- Zone 2 steady sessions: progressive increase from 25 min up to 50 min through the program with a deload every 4th week.
- HIIT: 1×/week, 20–30 min total session, only on non‑flow days. Examples:
  - Bike 8×20s work / 40s easy,
  - Row 6×45s work / 90s easy,
  - Pyramid intervals or EMOM combos.
- Flow days: restrict to Zone 1 walking, swimming, or gentle cycling for 15–30 min.

Plyometric / Power day (1×/week on Sat)
- Weeks 1–4: low volume, low‑impact power drills (medicine ball throws, low box jumps 15–30 cm or step‑downs, quick feet drills). Total jumps <12.
- Weeks 5–7: increase intensity on non‑flow days: drop jumps 20–30 cm, single‑leg bounds/hops (if comfortable), explosive trap‑bar shrugs — volume 12–20 quality attempts.
- Weeks 9–11: complex combos, med‑ball rotational throws, reactive drop jumps; maintain quality and safe landings.
- Week 8 and Week 12: deload and perform low‑impact alternatives if they coincide with flow (MB throws, band speed work, swim sprints).

Flow‑day modifications (any training during cycle days 1–3)
- Replace heavy lifts with:
  - Low‑load technical practice: bodyweight squats 3×10, banded hip hinges 3×12, glute bridges 3×15.
  - Low‑impact cardio: 15–30 min walking, easy cycling, or swimming (Zone 1).
  - Low‑impact power: medicine‑ball throws, light kettlebell swings, banded explosive step‑ups (no jumping).
  - Breathing & mobility: diaphragmatic breathing 5–10 min, pelvic floor awareness, heat pack recommendation.
- Do not perform HIIT, heavy singles requiring Valsalva, or plyometric jumps.

Nutrition plan summary (cycle‑aware; supports fatigue & cramping)
- Daily macronutrient guidance:
  - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily.
  - Fat: 25–35% of calories, emphasize omega‑3 sources (salmon, flax, walnuts).
  - Carbohydrates: periodized — higher on heavier training days and during follicular/luteal phases; slightly higher carbs on flow days to offset fatigue.
  - Calories: aim maintenance to slight surplus for recovery and strength gains. Avoid aggressive deficit, especially in luteal/menstrual window.
- Key nutrients and supplements (discuss with GP/RD):
  - Magnesium 200–400 mg at night may reduce cramps.
  - Omega‑3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA) may reduce pain/inflammation.
  - Iron only if labs indicate deficiency (check ferritin if heavy bleeding).
  - Vitamin D if deficient.
- Flow‑day eating strategies:
  - Warm meals, small frequent meals if nausea, focus on magnesium/iron rich foods, maintain hydration and electrolytes (salted broths if lightheaded).
  - Avoid excessive caffeine/alcohol around flow onset.
- Pre/post workout fueling:
  - Pre: small carb snack 30–60 min before higher‑intensity sessions.
  - Post: 20–40 g protein + carbs (30–60 g) after long or intense sessions.

HIIT integration & safety
- 1 HIIT session/week on non‑flow days only. If it coincides with flow, swap for Zone 1 recovery or light cardio.
- Keep session short (20–30 min) and low‑impact (bike/row/ski erg); emphasize breathing and avoid breath‑holding.
- Progress high‑effort time from ~6–8 min up to 10–12 min throughout 12 weeks, with deloads on Weeks 4, 8, 12.

Plyo integration & safety
- 1 plyo session/week on non‑flow days (Sat default). Swap to low‑impact power on flow weeks.
- Begin low volume, progress to moderate volume focused on quality and fast ground contact.
- Prioritize landing mechanics, full recovery between maximal attempts, and breathing.

1RM testing guidance (end of Phase 3)
- Test only on a non‑flow day. For the 12‑week plan:
  - Week 12 (08‑17 → 08‑23) includes flow 08‑21–08‑23, so DO NOT test on those dates.
  - Recommended testing window: pick a non‑flow day in Week 11 (08‑10 → 08‑16) or in the week after Week 12 (e.g., 08‑24 → 08‑30), depending on readiness.
- Prefer testing 1–2 lifts only (e.g., squat and deadlift on separate days with 48–72 hrs between). Use thorough warm‑up, small incremental jumps, spotters and safety.
- Consider 3‑RM or 5‑RM or velocity‑based estimates if you want lower risk.

Deload weeks and cycle alignment
- Deload on Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12 to align each month’s flow days with reduced training stress.
- Deload = reduce volume 40–50% and intensity 10–20% as needed. Use these weeks for recovery, mobility, and flow‑day symptom management.

Autoregulation & monitoring
- Use RPE, bar speed and symptom reporting each session. If cramping, dizziness, or excessive fatigue occurs, reduce load 10–20% and consider skipping HIIT/plyo.
- Keep a training + symptom log for each cycle to refine scheduling (heavy days vs. flow days) in future mesocycles.
- Communicate daily on cycle day 0–1 during flow to decide whether to proceed or scale back.

Quick checklist for each training day

- Flow‑day check: if cycle day 1–3, modify session per the flow‑day template.
- Breathing: coach controlled exhale on exertion; avoid Valsalva on flow days.
- Recovery: sleep 7–9 hrs, magnesium at night if helpful, hydration and carbs especially on heavy days.
